title: Data Analytics & Automation Specialist
desc: Hours: Full-Time – 35 Hours Work Location: 30-30 Thomson Avenue, LIC, NY 11101 The Technology and Innovation Division (T&I) within the New York City Department of Design and Construction (DDC) seeks to hire a skilled, data-driven Data Analytics & Automation Specialist. DDC is the City’s primary capital construction agency, responsible for delivering safe, sustainable, and innovative public buildings and infrastructure across the five boroughs. Partnering with client agencies, design professionals, and the construction industry, DDC manages a broad portfolio of projects from firehouses, libraries, and community centers to roadways, sewers, and resiliency initiatives helping to shape a more equitable, efficient, and resilient city. Through its commitment to design excellence, technological modernization, and public service, DDC ensures that critical civic projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest standards of quality. The Technology and Innovation (T&I) Division serves as DDC’s centralized Information, Technology, and Telecom operation, organized into four core units: Network, Infrastructure and Security; Service Delivery; Application Development, and Administrative Analytics. Together, these units provide the hardware, software, enterprise applications, and data ecosystem that support the agency’s daily operations. In addition to maintaining core systems, the division leads strategic modernization efforts aimed at improving efficiency, strengthening security, and advancing programmatic excellence across the agency. Reporting directly to the Director of Administrative Analytics, the Data Analytics & Automation Specialist will blend business intelligence and reporting with hands-on data engineering and automation. The selected candidate will build the dashboards leadership relies on and the automated pipelines that feed them across HR, budget, contracting, procurement, and other administrative functions. The ideal candidate will combine strong technical skills in business intelligence, SQL, Python, and automation with excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and will be comfortable working directly with non-technical users to gather requirements, conceptualize business challenges, and deliver practical solutions. This role involves working with sensitive and sometimes confidential data, including personnel information and internal agency operations. The selected candidate will emphasize security and access control in the design of pipelines, the distribution of reports and tools, and the infrastructure that hosts this data. The responsibilities include: - Design, develop, and maintain interactive dashboards, reports, and data visualizations using Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools, including recurring and ad hoc reporting for agency leadership. - Write and maintain SQL queries to extract, transform, validate, and analyze data from agency databases and citywide systems. - Develop Python scripts, ETL processes, and automated pipelines to integrate data from multiple sources, replace manual data handling, and improve the speed, reliability, and accuracy of reporting. - Design and build Power Automate workflows and Power Apps to automate multi-step administrative processes, such as approvals, tracking, and data intake, and integrate them with other agency systems. - Build and maintain data models and automated reporting processes to improve the reliability, efficiency, and integrity of administrative reporting. - Identify opportunities to leverage automation, advanced analytics, and emerging technologies to modernize administrative processes across the agency. title: Data Engineer
desc: The New York City Department of Sanitation (DSNY) keeps New York City healthy, safe, and clean by collecting, recycling, and disposing of waste, cleaning City streets and vacant lots, and clearing snow and ice. DSNY is the nation's largest municipal sanitation agency, with nearly 10,000 employees, 59 district garages, and a fleet of more than 5,000 trucks, cars, and other types of equipment. The Department clears litter, snow, and ice from approximately 6,500 miles of City streets and removes debris from vacant lots as well as abandoned vehicles from City streets. Under general supervision, with considerable latitude for the exercise of independent judgment and initiative, the incumbent will be responsible for the design, development, implementation, enhancement, documentation, and maintenance of database management systems, data integration solutions, custom applications, and related software functions supporting the Department of Sanitation's Operations Management Division (OMD). title: Analytics & Reporting Engineer for the Division of Strategic Operations & Analytics
desc: About the Agency: The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City. As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike. Your Team: The Office of Policy and Strategy (OPS) leverage its expertise to guide and support HPD and its many Offices in their efforts to deepen their impact, optimize their efficiency, and become more data-driven, climate-adaptive, and mission-focused. As part of OPS, the Division of Strategic Operations and Analytics (SOA) works to increase HPD's impact by analyzing and improving operations agency-wide. SOA does this by clarifying HPD program missions, objectives, and stakeholders; implementing initiatives that advance HPD's goals; analyzing data to deliver actionable insights to HPD programs; and increasing the agency's overall ability to leverage data. Your Impact: As the Analytics & Reporting Engineer within SOA, you will play a key role in making HPD’s data more accessible, reliable, and reusable to support reporting and analytics. By building well-structured datasets, automations and data flows, you will help SOA and other HPD offices turn data into key reporting and metrics that support key agency programs for New Yorkers. Your Role: Your role will focus on hands-on development of data pipelines, curating datasets and data flows in SQL Server and building reusable scripts and code to support reporting and analytics work for agency programs such as homeless placement services, homebuyer assistance, housing distress & compliance, and fair housing work. You will also create and maintain reports and dashboards, or related dataflows/models. title: Strategy Analyst
desc: Job Summary The Strategy Analyst supports executive and health system leadership across the enterprise by translating complex internal, market, and industry datasets into actionable strategic insights. Operating within the Business Development department, this role focuses on evaluating market share dynamics, optimizing ambulatory and inpatient access points, supporting service line planning, and supporting enterprise capacity planning. The ideal candidate combines strong quantitative modeling skills with healthcare domain fluency to inform capital allocation, network expansion, and long-term strategic planning. Essential Functions Market Share & Competitive Intelligence: Analyze external claims, state inpatient/outpatient discharge databases, and demographic data to evaluate market share trends, competitor positioning, migration patterns, and whitespace opportunities across primary and secondary service areas. Service Line Analytics: Partner with service line executives and physician leaders to assess clinical program performance, volume trajectories, payer mix shifts, contribution margins, and downstream referral patterns. Access Point & Network Optimization: Conduct geospatial and catchment area analyses to evaluate ambulatory footprint performance, site-of-care shifts, clinic utilization, and optimal locations for new facilities or service expansions. Capacity Planning & Demand Forecasting: Build quantitative models to project inpatient bed demand, procedural room utilization, and ambulatory capacity constraints based on population health trends, clinical acuity, and operational throughput. Executive Decision Support: Synthesize multi-source findings into clear, executive-ready presentations and business cases that guide strategic planning, partnership evaluations, and capital investments. ***Hybrid in Franklin, TN strongly preferred. Fully remote considered for standout candidates with exceptional experience*** Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Economics, Data Science, Finance, Statistics, Public Health, or a related quantitative field required; Master’s degree (MHA, MPH, MBA, or MS in Analytics) is strongly preferred. Experience: Minimum of 2–4 years of experience in healthcare strategy, management consulting, decision support, or quantitative analytics. Direct experience working within a hospital, multi-hospital health system, payer, or healthcare consulting environment strongly preferred. Technical Background: Experience working with large-scale healthcare datasets (e.g., Epic/Cerner EHR extracts, Cost Accounting/Decision Support systems, state/all-payer claims data, CMS datasets, or syndicated market intelligence platforms such as Sg2, Advisory Board, or Claritas). Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) Healthcare Domain Knowledge: Understanding of hospital and ambulatory operations, healthcare reimbursement models, service line economics (e.g., DRGs, APCs, RVUs), and competitive market dynamics. Analytical & Data Visualization Skills: Proficiency in Excel for complex data analysis and financial/volume modeling; demonstrated ability to build intuitive visuals in Tableau, Power BI, or Excel. Strategic Communication: Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint to design clean, structured, executive-ready slide decks. Ability to distill technical analyses into concise business narratives for executives, clinical leaders, and other non-technical stakeholders. Project Management & Collaboration: Self-directed with strong organizational skills to manage multiple competing strategic initiatives simultaneously while maintaining rigorous attention to analytical accuracy.
